chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Durust, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Aḥwal, from Ḥumrān who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): 'It has reached us that Hell will be filled until its gates are [crammed] shut.'
He said: 'No, by Allah, it is [going to remain as it is] for eternity!'
I asked: '[What about the verse that states:] [They will] remain therein forever, as long as the heavens and the earth will endure, except what your Lord wills (Q11:107)?'
He said: 'That is for those who will come out from the Fire [with the permission of Allah].'
ai.seo_question: Is Hell eternal or temporary according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the Shia doctrine of *Khulud* (eternity) versus *Khalad* (duration), affirming that while Hell is fundamentally eternal, a specific category of believers will be expelled from it. The Imam interprets the Quranic phrase 'as long as the heavens and the earth' not as a limit on Hell's existence, but as the temporal duration of the stay for those granted intercession, thereby reconciling the concept of permanent punishment with the possibility of release for the monotheists. This distinction is central to the Shia understanding of divine mercy overriding strict retributive justice for sinners who possess faith.
